title: Birds & Botanicals
description: The art of scientific observation — Audubon's birds and the great botanical plates.

items.title: John James Audubon discovering his drawings eaten by a rat
items.description_narrative: This vibrant color woodblock print captures naturalist John James Audubon's dramatic discovery of a rat consuming his invaluable avian drawings. The vivid scene, characteristic of the medium, portrays a moment of profound artistic and scientific loss.
items.tags: john james audubon, rat, naturalist, discovery, woodblock print, 19th century, dramatic, frustration

items.title: Harlequin Duck
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving with aquatint and etching on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This vibrant hand-colored engraving captures the distinctive Harlequin Duck, showcasing intricate detail through aquatint and etching techniques. Created by Robert Havell, it exemplifies the detailed natural history illustrations of the early 19th century.
items.tags: harlequin duck, bird, wildlife, natural history, engraving, aquatint, etching, hand-colored

items.title: Black Backed Gull
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving with aquatint and etching on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: This print, titled 'Black Backed Gull,' is a meticulous ornithological illustration by Robert Havell. Created through hand-colored engraving with aquatint and etching, the artwork captures the bird's form and plumage with precise line work and subtle tonal variations.
items.tags: ornithology, bird, nature, engraving, aquatint, hand-colored, printmaking, detailed

items.title: Great American Shrike
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving, with aquatint, on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This hand-colored engraving by Robert Havell meticulously depicts the Great American Shrike, showcasing the artist's skill in combining line and aquatint. The detailed rendering of the bird on ivory wove paper serves as both scientific illustration and fine art.
items.tags: bird, engraving, ornithological, nature, scientific illustration, printmaking, natural history

items.title: Male Bay Breasted Warbler
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving, with aquatint, on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: This exquisite hand-colored engraving by Robert Havell vividly captures the intricate details of a male Bay-breasted Warbler. Rendered with aquatint on cream wove paper, the print showcases the bird's distinctive plumage and a delicate branch.
items.tags: bird, warbler, nature, engraving, hand-colored, ornithological illustration, 19th century

items.title: Florida Jay
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving, with aquatint, on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Robert Havell's 'Florida Jay' is a meticulously hand-colored engraving, capturing the distinctive plumage of the Florida Scrub-Jay. This detailed aquatint print exemplifies the artistic and scientific precision characteristic of early 19th-century ornithological illustration.
items.tags: bird, wildlife, natural history, engraving, hand-colored print, scientific illustration, 19th century

items.title: Cervus Virginianus
items.description_narrative: This hand-colored lithograph by John Woodhouse Audubon vividly portrays the Cervus Virginianus, commonly known as the white-tailed deer, with careful attention to naturalistic detail. The intricate rendition and hand-coloring highlight the animal's features, reflecting the era's focus on detailed natural history illustration.
items.tags: deer, wildlife, animal illustration, lithography, hand-colored, 19th century, natural history

items.title: Bust of a Youth (Saint John the Baptist)
items.medium: Marble on variegated black marble socle
items.description_narrative: Francesco Mochi's marble 'Bust of a Youth' vividly portrays Saint John the Baptist, capturing a moment of profound spiritual intensity. The dynamic carving of the youthful figure, along with its expressive face, exemplifies the dramatic potential of Baroque sculpture.
items.tags: sculpture, marble, baroque, religious, saint john the baptist, bust, dramatic, expressive

items.title: Saint James the Greater
items.medium: Etching in black on cream laid paper
items.description_narrative: This etching in black on cream laid paper depicts Saint James the Greater, an important figure in Christian tradition. Created by the artist known as Master F. P., the print showcases the precise lines achievable through this medium.
items.tags: saint james, religious, christian, etching, printmaking, figurative, devotional

items.title: Saint John the Evangelist
items.description_narrative: This etching by Paolo Farinati depicts Saint John the Evangelist, showcasing the characteristic linework of the printmaking medium. Created in 1567, it reflects the artistic approaches of its era.
items.tags: saint, biblical, etching, printmaking, renaissance art, religious, italian art

items.title: Nocturne: Blue and Gold—Southampton Water
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas by James McNeill Whistler captures the tranquil expanse of Southampton Water under a moonlit or twilight sky. Through a masterful blend of blues and golds, Whistler transforms the landscape into an ethereal study of atmosphere and color harmony, emphasizing beauty over literal depiction.
items.tags: nocturne, seascape, aestheticism, atmospheric, tonalism, blue and gold, tranquility

items.title: At Mouquin's
items.description_narrative: William Glackens's 'At Mouquin's' captures a lively restaurant interior, depicting patrons engaged in dining and conversation. Rendered in oil on canvas, this 1905 work exemplifies a candid observation of urban life.
items.tags: restaurant, urban life, genre scene, american art, ashcan school, early 20th century, social realism

items.title: Butterfly
items.description_narrative: This delicate drawing, titled 'Butterfly,' is rendered in graphite by James McNeill Whistler, capturing the subtle form of the insect. Executed on ivory wove paper, it exemplifies a precise and refined approach to natural observation.
items.tags: butterfly, insect, drawing, graphite, sketch, nature, study, aesthetic

items.title: Plaque with Saints James and John the Evangelist
items.description_narrative: This plaque depicts Saints James and John the Evangelist, crafted from gilt copper with champlevé enamel. The intricate enamelwork, created by carving recesses into the metal and filling them with colored glass paste, exemplifies the decorative artistry of its period.
items.tags: religious, medieval, champlevé, enamel, metalwork, saints, decorative arts

items.title: James William Wallack
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting by Charles Robert Leslie depicts James William Wallack. Created between 1835 and 1840, it showcases Leslie's skill as a portraitist.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, 19th century, male figure, charles robert leslie, james william wallack, american art, british art

items.title: Mary (Polly) Lawton Bringhurst
items.medium: Watercolor on ivory (recto), sepia on ivory with human hair (verso), and gold
items.description_narrative: This exquisite miniature portrait depicts Mary (Polly) Lawton Bringhurst, rendered in watercolor on ivory by James Peale. The artwork's intricate design extends to the verso, which features sepia on ivory adorned with human hair and encased in gold.
items.tags: portrait, miniature, watercolor, ivory, sepia, 18th century, american

items.title: Head of Executioner, from John Evelyn's Sculptura
items.medium: Mezzotint in black on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: This mezzotint depicts the powerful "Head of Executioner," rendered in stark black on ivory laid paper. Created by Richard Houston in 1755, it showcases the detailed textural qualities possible with this printmaking technique.
items.tags: executioner, head, portrait, mezzotint, printmaking, 18th century, british

items.title: Design cover for West Point Song of the Graduates
items.medium: Transfer lithograph in black on off-white wove paper
items.description_narrative: James McNeill Whistler designed this cover for the "West Point Song of the Graduates," an early example of his work in printmaking. Rendered as a transfer lithograph in black on off-white wove paper, this piece demonstrates Whistler's nascent skills in commercial design.
items.tags: west point, song cover, military, lithography, design, illustration, american art

items.title: Lady Elizabeth Montagu
items.description_narrative: This elegant mezzotint depicts Lady Elizabeth Montagu, a prominent figure in 18th-century English society known for her literary salons. James McArdell masterfully uses the mezzotint technique to achieve rich tonal variations, creating a sophisticated portrait.
items.tags: portrait, woman, nobility, 18th century, mezzotint, printmaking, elegant, British art

items.title: Title Page, from A select collection of views and ruins in Rome and its vicinity
items.description_narrative: This intricately designed title page introduces 'A select collection of views and ruins in Rome and its vicinity,' an album showcasing the enduring grandeur of Roman architecture. Executed as a hand-colored aquatint, it offers an artistic prelude to the detailed topographical prints within the publication.
items.tags: title page, aquatint, roman ruins, topographical, 18th century, hand-colored, printmaking

items.title: Coverlet
items.medium: Cotton and wool, plain weave double cloth; woven on loom with Jacquard attachment; two loom widths joined
items.description_narrative: This coverlet, crafted by James Cunningham in 1843, demonstrates the intricate possibilities of double-cloth weaving using cotton and wool. Its creation on a loom with a Jacquard attachment highlights early mechanical advancements in textile production, resulting in two joined loom widths.
items.tags: coverlet, textile, weaving, jacquard, cotton, wool, domestic art, 19th century

items.title: James Vibert, Sculptor
items.description_narrative: Ferdinand Hodler's 1907 oil on canvas presents a portrait titled 'James Vibert, Sculptor'. The painting depicts the sculptor James Vibert, created by Hodler, and serves as an example of his portraiture.
items.tags: portraiture, male subject, sculptor, oil painting, 1907, ferdinand hodler

items.title: The Fountain, Villa Torlonia, Frascati, Italy
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent captures the grand fountain at Villa Torlonia in Frascati, Italy. The artwork masterfully renders the play of light and shadow across the water and surrounding classical architecture.
items.tags: landscape, Italy, fountain, villa, oil painting, light, Edwardian, architecture

items.title: Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: This tempera on panel artwork, 'Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist,' was created by Bartolomeo di Giovanni. Dating from around 1490–95, it vividly depicts significant moments from the saint's life.
items.tags: religious, narrative, early renaissance, italian, tempera, saint john the baptist

items.title: Stoke-by-Nayland
items.description_narrative: John Constable's "Stoke-by-Nayland" depicts a familiar rural English landscape, rendered with his characteristic attention to natural light and atmospheric conditions. This oil on canvas masterwork captures the vastness of the Suffolk countryside under a dynamic sky, reflecting Constable's deep connection to his native region.
items.tags: landscape, romanticism, england, nature, rural, atmospheric, 19th century

items.title: Landscape with Saint John on Patmos
items.description_narrative: Nicolas Poussin's "Landscape with Saint John on Patmos" depicts the evangelist on the island of Patmos, a traditional setting for the writing of the Book of Revelation. The scene is presented as an idealized classical landscape, reflecting Poussin's characteristic approach to integrating figures within grand, structured natural environments.
items.tags: landscape, religious, classical, baroque, serene, saint john, patmos

items.title: Mrs. George Swinton (Elizabeth Ebsworth)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 1897 portrait of Mrs. George Swinton captures her elegant pose and sophisticated attire. This oil on canvas exemplifies Sargent's mastery of society portraiture and his distinctive brushwork.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, society portraiture, gilded age, elegance, late 19th century, realism, london society

items.title: The Captive Slave (Ira Aldridge)
items.description_narrative: This 1827 oil on canvas by John Philip Simpson portrays Ira Aldridge, an African American actor, in a poignant dramatic role as a captive slave. The artwork captures a moment of intense emotion, reflecting themes of bondage and human dignity.
items.tags: portrait, slavery, Ira Aldridge, acting, oil painting, 19th century, dramatic, realism

items.title: Rip Van Winkle
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts a scene from Washington Irving's classic American short story, 'Rip Van Winkle,' first published in 1819. John Quidor frequently drew inspiration from literary sources, bringing narrative depth to his canvases.
items.tags: american painting, romanticism, literature, folklore, narrative, oil painting

items.title: Coast Scene, Bathers
items.description_narrative: James McNeill Whistler's 'Coast Scene, Bathers' presents a tranquil view of figures along a shoreline. Executed in oil on panel, the work exemplifies his nuanced approach to color and atmosphere, capturing the subtle interplay of light and water.
items.tags: seascape, bathers, shoreline, tonalism, aestheticism, oil painting, 19th century, serene

items.title: Grey and Silver: Old Battersea Reach
items.description_narrative: This painting captures a serene view of the Thames at Battersea Reach, rendered in Whistler's characteristic muted tones of grey and silver. The work exemplifies his exploration of atmospheric effects and tonal harmony, reducing elements to evocative visual poetry.
items.tags: river scene, London, tonalism, aestheticism, urban landscape, boats, serene, subtle

items.title: The Artist in His Studio
items.medium: Oil on paper mounted on panel
items.description_narrative: James McNeill Whistler's 'The Artist in His Studio' offers an intimate glimpse into a painter's private creative space. Rendered in oil on paper mounted on panel, the work subtly reveals details of the artistic environment during the mid-19th century.
items.tags: artist, studio, interior, oil painting, 19th century, american art, british art

items.title: Mrs. John Nicholson (Hannah Duncan) and John Nicholson, Jr.
items.description_narrative: This double portrait by Charles Willson Peale depicts Hannah Duncan Nicholson and her son, John Nicholson, Jr., capturing a tender familial moment. Painted in oil on canvas in 1790, it exemplifies Peale's skill in rendering lifelike figures and intimate domestic scenes.
items.tags: portrait, mother and child, family, 18th century, american art, oil painting, realism, domestic scene

items.title: Arrangement in Flesh Color and Brown: Portrait of Arthur Jerome Eddy
items.description_narrative: This striking oil portrait, titled "Arrangement in Flesh Color and Brown," captures Arthur Jerome Eddy with an emphasis on color harmony rather than detailed representation. Created by James McNeill Whistler in 1894, it exemplifies his innovative approach to portraiture as a study in tonal relationships and artistic arrangement.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, whistler, tonalism, aestheticism, fin de siècle, american art

items.title: Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's oil on canvas portrait of Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre) captures the sitter with characteristic elegance and directness. Painted in 1882, the work exemplifies Sargent's mastery of light and texture in rendering a commanding social presence.
items.tags: portrait, woman, society portraiture, realism, elegant, 19th century, american art

items.title: Icebound
items.description_narrative: John Henry Twachtman's 'Icebound' captures a serene winter landscape, likely reflecting the artist's home in Greenwich, Connecticut. The composition features a muted palette and delicate brushwork, evoking the quiet beauty and reflective atmosphere of a snow-covered scene.
items.tags: winter, landscape, snow, ice, impressionism, american impressionism, serene, subtle
